newsitem.title: LATVIA: UNIBANKA SEEN RECOVERING BUT SHARES SEEN QUIET.
newsitem.headline: UNIBANKA SEEN RECOVERING BUT SHARES SEEN QUIET.

text.p: Leading share Unibanka is seen recovering next week after the news of its cancelled merger with Zemes Banka but total share trade is expected to be quiet amid many shareholder meetings, analysts and dealers said Thursday.
"The cancelled merger with Zemes Banka is good news for Unibanka as a stock," one analyst said.
"The merger would have meant a lost year in terms of expanding its market share," he added.
"I do not think, that the bank needed it (the merger) really, given the current pace of development of the banking sector," he added.
Other market participants were also confident on Unibanka.
"Following a short pause, Unibanka will continue its movement upwards," Dmitri Krutik, head of Rietumu Banka's securities department, said in an analysis.
"The state of Unibanka, according to a number of experts, is better than in Zemes," Krutik added.
For the market as a whole, no major change in activity is expected in the weeks after the Easter vacation as many shareholder meetings are held and share are blocked in accounts.
"We might get only slightly bigger activity next week," one dealer said.

Valmiera Glassfibre, which fluctuated during the week between two lats and 1.87 lats, is expected to become more stable as the company's shares become concentrated in fewer hands, Rietumu's Krutik said in his analysis.
Riga Shipyard, planning to join the market in April, is seen as a business with good prospects within its regional niche, said one analyst.
